issues.description: CHANGELOG entry name does not match the actual check directory/ID
issues.detail: The PR title and description say the check is `compute_image_publicly_shared`, but the directory and class are `compute_image_not_publicly_shared`. The CHANGELOG entry uses `compute_image_not_publicly_shared`, which matches the code, but the PR description is inconsistent. More importantly, ensure metadata.json `CheckID` matches the file/folder name exactly — it does here, but verify documentation/PR description is corrected before merge to avoid downstream confusion.

issues.description: `_get_images` lists all images including Google-managed/public images by default
issues.detail: `images().list(project=project_id)` returns custom images owned by the project, but the description claims only custom images are evaluated. Worth confirming behavior — the API will not return public Google images for someone else's project, but if `project_id` happens to be `debian-cloud` etc. it would. Consider filtering by `family`/source or documenting the assumption.

issues.description: Per-image getIamPolicy errors are logged but image still appears as not publicly shared
issues.detail: If `getIamPolicy` raises (e.g., permission denied as in test-image-3), `publicly_shared` remains False and the image is appended. The check will then report PASS for an image whose policy could not be read, hiding a true public-share. Consider skipping the image, marking as unknown, or surfacing an error state instead of a false PASS.

issues.description: Images fetched serially per project instead of via `__threading_call__`
issues.detail: All other resource collectors in `__init__` use `__threading_call__`, but `_get_images()` iterates projects sequentially and additionally makes one `getIamPolicy` call per image serially. For accounts with many projects/images this will be noticeably slow and inconsistent with the surrounding service. Consider parallelizing across `project_ids`.

issues.description: Reliance on `error.__traceback__.tb_lineno` will crash if traceback is None
issues.detail: If an exception is raised without an attached traceback (rare but possible via `raise SomeError()` re-raised from a context without traceback, or in tests using `Exception()` directly), `error.__traceback__` may be None and `.tb_lineno` will AttributeError inside the except handler. Other handlers in this file appear to use the same pattern, so this is a pre-existing nit, but the new code copies it.

issues.description: Required IAM permissions for `compute.images.getIamPolicy` not documented
issues.detail: The PR checklist explicitly asks whether provider permissions need updating. This check requires `compute.images.list` and `compute.images.getIamPolicy`. Confirm Prowler's documented GCP role/permission set already includes `getIamPolicy` on images, or update it; otherwise users will see widespread permission-denied logs and silent PASS results.

review.summary: The new GCP check is well-structured and tested, but has a few non-trivial concerns. The most important is that `getIamPolicy` errors cause images to be reported as PASS (not publicly shared) when their policy could not actually be read, which can hide real exposures — the test fixture for image-3 even exercises this silent-PASS path. Image collection is also serial across projects unlike all other collectors in `compute_service.py`. Smaller items: PR description vs. actual check name mismatch, no apparent update to required GCP IAM permissions for `compute.images.getIamPolicy`, and traceback access pattern.
